title: Sustainable Development Goal 1 (SDG 1): Eradicating Poverty Through Goat Farming
excerpt: SDG 1 aims to eradicate extreme poverty for all people everywhere. In Puti-Puti subcounty, Buyesi Youth Initiative is turning this global goal into local reality through sustainable goat farming.
content:
No Poverty — A Global Goal, A Local Mission

Sustainable Development Goal 1 (SDG 1) aims to eradicate extreme poverty for all people everywhere by 2030. While this is a global ambition, its realization depends on grassroots action — and that is exactly where Buyesi Youth Initiative steps in.

In Puti-Puti subcounty, Pallisa District, Eastern Uganda, poverty is not an abstract statistic. It is the reality faced by thousands of families who struggle daily to meet basic needs — food, healthcare, and education for their children. The unemployment rate among youth is alarmingly high, and traditional farming methods often fail to generate enough income to break the cycle of poverty.

The Goat Economy: A Pathway Out of Poverty

At Buyesi Youth Initiative, we believe that goat farming offers one of the most practical and sustainable pathways out of poverty for rural communities. A single goat can transform a family's economic outlook through multiple revenue streams:

  • Meat production: Goat meat is in high demand across Uganda and the broader East African region, providing reliable income at market.
  • Milk: Goat milk is a nutritious, high-value product that serves both household nutrition needs and commercial sale.
  • Hides and skins: These by-products are processed into leather goods, adding another income stream for farming families.
  • Manure: Goat manure is an excellent organic fertilizer that improves crop yields, reducing the need for expensive chemical inputs.

From Dependence to Self-Sufficiency

Our approach goes beyond simply distributing goats. We provide comprehensive training in modern goat husbandry, covering nutrition, housing, disease prevention, and breeding techniques. Through our demonstration farm, farmers learn hands-on skills that they can immediately apply to their own herds.

The pass-on-the-gift model ensures that the impact multiplies: when a family's goat produces offspring, they pass on a kid to a neighbouring family, creating a ripple effect of empowerment across the community.

Real Impact, Real Lives

Since our founding, we have seen families go from struggling to feed themselves to sending their children to school, accessing healthcare, and building permanent homes — all from the income generated by goat farming. These are not just numbers; these are lives transformed.

SDG 1 calls on all of us to act. At Buyesi Youth Initiative, we are answering that call one goat at a time. Together, we can eradicate poverty in Puti-Puti and beyond.

title: In the Remote Village of Mpongi: How Goat Farming Is Changing Lives in Pallisa District
excerpt: In the remote village known as Mpongi, found in Pallisa District, Eastern Uganda, families are discovering a new path to prosperity through community-driven goat farming.
content:
A Village Transformed

In the remote village known as Mpongi, found in Pallisa District, Eastern Uganda, life has long revolved around subsistence farming. Families here depend on small plots of land, growing just enough maize, millet, and cassava to survive. Cash income is scarce, and opportunities for youth are even scarcer. But something remarkable is beginning to change.

Through the Buyesi Youth Initiative's goat farming program, families in Mpongi are discovering a new path to prosperity — one that is sustainable, community-driven, and deeply rooted in local traditions.

Why Mpongi?

Mpongi represents hundreds of similar villages across Eastern Uganda where poverty, limited infrastructure, and lack of market access keep families trapped in cycles of deprivation. The village has no reliable electricity, limited access to clean water, and the nearest health centre is several kilometres away. For the youth, the choice has often been stark: stay and struggle, or migrate to the cities in search of uncertain opportunities.

Buyesi Youth Initiative chose to work in Mpongi precisely because of these challenges. We believe that sustainable change must begin in the places where it is needed most.

The Program in Action

Our work in Mpongi began with community meetings — listening to the needs, concerns, and aspirations of village members. From these conversations, a clear picture emerged: families wanted a reliable source of income that did not depend on unpredictable weather or distant markets.

Goat farming was the natural answer. Goats are well-suited to the local environment, require relatively modest investment, and reproduce quickly. Within a year, a family can go from owning a single goat to managing a small herd.

We provided initial breeding stock to selected families, along with intensive training on:

  • Proper housing: Building simple but effective shelters that protect goats from disease and predators.
  • Nutrition: Using locally available feeds and supplements to ensure healthy growth and reproduction.
  • Disease management: Identifying common goat diseases early and administering basic treatments.
  • Breeding: Selecting the best animals for breeding to improve herd quality over generations.

Early Results

The results have been encouraging. Within the first year, participating families reported increased household income, improved nutrition from goat milk, and a growing sense of hope for the future. Children who had previously dropped out of school due to lack of fees are now returning to the classroom, funded by income from goat sales.

Perhaps most importantly, the program has sparked a sense of community solidarity. Families share knowledge, help each other with veterinary care, and celebrate each other's successes. The pass-on-the-gift model — where families share offspring with their neighbours — has created a web of mutual support that extends far beyond the original beneficiaries.

Looking Ahead

Mpongi is just the beginning. The lessons we are learning here — about community engagement, sustainable farming practices, and the transformative power of goat farming — will guide our expansion into other villages across Pallisa District and beyond.

Every goat we distribute, every farmer we train, and every family we empower brings us one step closer to our vision: a rural Uganda where no family is left behind.

title: Launching a UK Charity to Secure Long-Term Funding for the Buyesi Goat Economy
excerpt: We are establishing a UK-based foundation to provide sustainable, long-term funding for the Buyesi Rural Breeding Model and our Every Goat, Every Child's Future programme.
content:
A New Chapter for Buyesi

Buyesi Youth Initiative is taking a bold step forward. We are in the process of establishing a UK-based charitable foundation — a dedicated fundraising vehicle that will provide sustainable, long-term funding for our community programmes in Pallisa and the wider Bukedi Region of Eastern Uganda.

This is not just another fundraiser. It is the foundation upon which we will build the future of the Buyesi Goat Economy and secure the resources needed to transform thousands of lives.

Why a UK Charity?

Our work on the ground in Uganda has proven that the Rural Breeding Model works. Families who receive quality breeding goats, combined with training in modern husbandry, are seeing real improvements in income, nutrition, and educational outcomes for their children. But to scale this impact — to reach more villages, train more farmers, and support more children — we need a reliable, transparent, and internationally recognised funding structure.

A UK-registered charity provides exactly that. It offers:

  • Credibility and trust: Donors and institutional funders can give with confidence, knowing their contributions are governed by UK charity law and subject to rigorous oversight.
  • Gift Aid: UK taxpayers who donate can boost their contribution by 25% through Gift Aid at no extra cost to themselves.
  • Access to grants: Many foundations, trusts, and government aid programmes only fund registered charities, opening doors that are currently closed to us.
  • Long-term sustainability: Rather than relying on one-off donations, a formal charity structure allows us to build recurring revenue, develop partnerships, and plan for the future with certainty.

What the Funds Will Cover

  • Legal advice and charity registration: Ensuring we meet all regulatory requirements from day one.
  • Financial administration: Setting up proper accounting, reporting, and compliance systems.
  • Communications materials: Building a professional presence — website, due-diligence documentation, and donor engagement tools.
  • Transparent monitoring systems: Leveraging our mobile app and child-tracking data to show donors exactly where their money goes.

We are committed to keeping startup costs lean through pro-bono support and volunteer time, ensuring that every pound raised is used wisely.

The Bigger Picture: Every Goat, Every Child's Future

The UK charity will be the primary funding channel for two flagship programmes:

The Rural Breeding Model organises farmers into groups of ten, provides purebred stock and training, and systematically improves local herd genetics over time. This is the economic engine — the goat economy in action.

Every Goat, Every Child's Future links livestock directly to children's education. Vulnerable children receive goats, mentorship, and school support, combining livestock income with learning to prepare them as future entrepreneurs and community leaders.

Together, these programmes address the root causes of poverty — not with handouts, but with assets, skills, and opportunity.

How You Can Help

We need your support to make this happen. The full programme budget targets $226,320 across our core initiatives, but right now, the most important step is getting the UK charity off the ground.

Together, we are not just raising money. We are building the infrastructure for lasting change.

title: Integrating Sustainable Goat Farming Practices with Education
content:
It was a happy moment to have smiles on children's faces. They were extremely excited to attend their first goat farming session.

The Every Goat Every Child's future does not only

donate goats to children but also train, mentor and

inspire them into sustainable goat farming practices. Our aim is to see our children become educated commercial goat farmers contributing greatly to the sustainability of their respective rural communities.

Practical and theoretical involvement of children in this creates a huge impact in as far as understanding goat farming, and it's dynamics is concerned.

Join the movement: send us a message at, info@buyesi.org

title: Herd Growth & Multiplication
content:
Glad to announce that our children have started growing their respective herd.

Recently in August, Michael received a goat through the Every Goat Every Child's Future program.

Michael is so passionate and his goat was able to give birth to two babies. This is wonderful. We look forward to impacting many more children in sustainable goat farming practices as they grow their herd.

Become part of the movement. Let’s Grow with Goats.

title: Rebecca, another young Goat Farmer created.
content:
Every Goat Every Child's Future.

Amazing to see Rebecca begin her journey in sustainable goat farming. A new young goat Farmer made.

Buyesi Youth Initiative continues to empower many more children in rural communities through donating Goats to them. Our aim is to establish a Sustainable and Generational Goat Economy, where traditional goat farming practices have been replaced by sustainable and commercial goat farming methods.

Several developmental programs have always left children behind regarding socio-economic transformation and development, yet children too contribute to generational economic wellness in rural communities as they imitate change and always willing to learn.

Let's join the movement to empower many more of our children in programs that grow our societies. Goat farming is one that changes lives and improves livelihoods.

Grow with Goats.

title: The Chefs Forum Student Pastry Chef 2026
content:
Buyesi Youth Initiative (BYI), sponsored by The Chefs' Forum was proud to attend the Chef's Forum Student Pastry Chef of the Year Final Event 2026 .

Inspiring to see young chefs showcase creativity, passion, and skill. Events like this remind us why empowering young people through opportunity, education and food systems matters so much.

The future is bright.

We were proud to share the BYl message during the event and connect with people who believe in empowerment through food, education community development and Every opportunity to learn, connect, and grow brings us one step closer to creating lasting impact.

Let’s Grow with Goats

title: Preparing for Buyesi at Crystal Palace Park, London
excerpt: This September we land in London for an afternoon of Ugandan cuisine, talks, art and a fundraising auction in support of the Buyesi Project.
content:
This September, the Buyesi Project comes to Crystal Palace Park in London for an afternoon of food, conversation and community. The exact date will be confirmed shortly — but preparation is already well underway.

Behind the scenes we're working with chefs to design a menu rooted in Ugandan cuisine, lining up speakers to share the story of the Goat Economy and the Rural Breeding Model, and curating a collection of prints and drawings for our fundraising auction. Every pound raised goes directly into goats, schooling and mentorship for children in rural Pallisa.

We're grateful to the Chefs Forum for their support in bringing this event together.

If you'd like to attend, partner with us, or contribute to the auction, get in touch via our contact page — or stand with us long-term by becoming a Goat Guardian.

See you in September.

title: Become a Goat Guardian — now live on buyesi.org
excerpt: Our Goat Guardian programme is now live on the website. You can donate directly and stand alongside a rural family in Uganda.
content:
We're delighted to share that the Goat Guardian programme is now live on buyesi.org/support — and you can donate directly from the page.

Becoming a Goat Guardian funds a complete package for a child in rural Uganda: a local goat, schooling essentials, ongoing mentorship, and an enduring relationship as the herd grows. In return, every Guardian receives their own Guardian ID (e.g. GG/01), a Buyesi shirt, regular progress updates, and invitations to our events and welfare initiatives.

It's the simplest, most direct way to stand with a rural family in Pallisa today. Visit the Become a Goat Guardian page to choose a tier and donate.

Thank you for walking alongside us.

title: Every Goat Every Child’s Future
content:
